theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Highest momentum rank (1.655) with the broadest eligible breadth (0.556) and non-crowded positioning (z=0.9), but hurst_tag is mean-revert and the detector's rank-IC is ~0. The only defensible lean is trend-following with an absolute-trend gate: stay exposed while eligible and breadth holds, not because it will outperform.
evidence: backtest_verdict: absolute-trend gate validated for drawdown control
theses.dissent: Mean-revert Hurst tag plus near-zero rank-IC suggests this leadership is fragile and could roll over quickly if global copper sentiment cools; best entry may already be behind.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Challenger theme at score 1.545, close margin to the leader (0.11), highest durability_bar among leaders (0.61), eligible, non-crowded (z=0.97). Rotation is broad (0.56 eligible) but directional=false, so this is a conditional relative-strength lean within commodities, not a handoff call.
theses.dissent: Energy is a crowded macro trade globally and the detector gives no forward edge on rotation timing — oil-specific oversupply news could break this theme independently of TSX breadth.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO lags the S&P/TSX composite by 6% over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Only theme flagged crowded=true (z=1.16) with negative score (-0.21) despite being eligible. Crowding is a size-down/avoid caution, NOT a fade or short. The guardrails explicitly forbid fading on crowding, but an avoid lean on a crowded, negatively-scored theme aligns with the drawdown-control mandate.
evidence: guardrails: crowding is a SIZE-DOWN caution only, never a fade
theses.dissent: Tech could mean-revert or benefit from rate-sensitive rallies given its mixed Hurst tag; avoiding it while eligible sacrifices any sharp bounce if sentiment flips.

falsifier.text: XIT.TO gains 5% relative to the S&P/TSX composite and crowding_z drops below 0.5 before the check-by date
